texts.preamble: Complainant vs Adesh Bansal on 26 July, 2022 In The Court Of Ms. Nabeela Wali Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate-01 New Delhi District, Patiala House Courts: New Delhi In the matter of : Cc No. :- 44284/16 Food Inspector Department of Pfa Govt of Nct of Delhi A-20 Lawrence Road Industrial Area Delhi-110035 .... Complainant Versus Adesh Bansal S/o Late Sh. S. N Bansal M/s Bansal Corner, 22, Central Market Ashok Vihar, Phase-1, Delhi-110052 R/o C-10, Ashok Vihar, Phase-I Delhi-110052 .... Vendor-cum-Proprietor Judgment
texts.facts: The present complaint has been filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as PFA Act), alleging that the accused has violated the provisions of the PFA Act and Rules. 2. As per the complaint, on 04.11.2010 at about 06:00 PM, Food Inspector (herein after referred to as 'FI') Ms. Usha Kiran, under the supervision/directions of Sh. Pardeep Baijal, SDM/LHA visited the premises of M/s Bansal Corner, 22, Central Market, Ashok Vihar, Phase-I, Delhi-110052. Accused Adesh Bansal was found conducting the business at the said shop, having stored various food articles including "Chocopie" for sale for human consumption. A sample consisting of 3x336g (12 packets) of "Chocopie" having label declaration 'ready for sale' was taken for inspection. Vide report dated 08.12.2010, the PA reported that the sample was misbranded because there is CC No:- 44284/2016 DA (FSO) v. Adesh Bansal Page No. 2 of 14 violation of Rule 32(c) (iii), Rule 32(i) and Rule 64-BB of PFA Act and Rules, 1955. The public analyst has also reported in his above stated report regarding label, without declaration of importer's address, expiration date given as 15 months from production and flavour declared as vanilla (artificial). However the sample was not adulterated. Hence, the present complaint was filed. 3. Since the complaint was filed by a public servant in writing, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 24.03.2011. 4. On appearing before the Court, accused was admitted to bail and provided with copy of complaint. He was served with notice under Section 251 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as 'Cr.P.C') on 22.07.2011 for offences punishable under Section of PFA Act and Rules, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. COMPLAINANT EVIDENCE 5. At the trial, the complainant department i.e. the prosecution examined four witnesses in support of its case. Sh. Pradeep, Retired SDM/LHA, Government of NCT of Delhi was examined as PW-1. PW-1 in his examination-in-chief stated CC No:- 44284/2016 DA (FSO) v. Adesh Bansal Page No. 3 of 14 that after lifting of sample, it was divided into three parts as per procedure prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules and separately packed and sealed. Necessary documents were prepared at the spot including the vendor's receipt, Notice in Form-VI (on which the label declarations of the food article were reproduced) and panchnama. As per PW-1 on 06.11.2010, one counterpart of the sample was deposited with the Public Analyst (PA) and remaining two counterparts were deposited with the LHA. As per PW-1, based on the report of PA, investigation was carried out by the Food Inspector on his instructions of the LHA. As per the witness after obtaining due sanction of the Director, PFA the present complaint was filed against the accused persons. PW-1 exhibited the following documents i.e. 1. Ex. PW 1/A : Vendor's Receipt; 2. Ex. PW 1/B : Notice in Form VI; Complainant vs Adesh Bansal on 26 July, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22060283/ 2 3. Ex. PW 1/C : Panchnama; 4. Ex. PW 1/D : Report under Rule 9(e); 5. Ex. PW 1/E : LHA receipt; 6. Ex. PW 1/F : PA Report; 7. Ex. PW 1/G : Consent for prosecution; 8. Ex. PW 1/H : Present complaint; 9. Mark-X : Photocopy of intimation letter; 10. Mark-X1 : Photocopies of postal registration receipts. CC No:- 44284/2016 DA (FSO) v. Adesh Bansal Page No. 4 of 14 6. PW-1 was duly cross-examined by counsel for accused. During cross-examination PW-1 could not recollect whether the manufacturing date and MRP was mentioned on the label of the sample commodity or not. He admitted that accused was not the manufacturer of the sample commodity and was only selling the sample commodity. 7. Ms. Usha Rani, Food Safety Officer, who was part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings was examined as PW-2. PW-2 deposed on similar lines as PW-1 and corroborated his version. She deposed that during sample proceedings she tried to associate customers, passers-by and neighbours but none came forward and hence FA Manhor Lal joined as a witness. PW-2 was cross examined by counsel for the accused and admitted that the sample commodity was originally in a sealed packet when it was lifted. 8. Sh. O. P. S. Ahlawat, Designated Officer was examined as PW- 3. He deposed that he carried out further investigation with respect to constitution of M/s Bansal Corner and relied upon the following documents i.e. 2. Ex. PW 3/B & : Letters sent to the accused/vendor Ex. PW 3/B-1 CC No:- 44284/2016 DA (FSO) v. Adesh Bansal Page No. 5 of 14 3. Ex. PW 3/C : Intimation letter personally served upon the accused. 4. Ex. PW 3/D (OSR) : Photocopies of postal registration receipts. 9. He also relied upon the documents Ex. PW 1/G and Ex. PW 1/H. However, PW-3 could not be cross-examined by the accused as he had subsequently expired and his name was dropped from the Complainant vs Adesh Bansal on 26 July, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22060283/ 3 list of witnesses. 10. Sh. S. M. Bhardwaj, Food Analyst was examined as PW-4. He deposed that on 06.11.2010, he received a sample of chocopie in sealed condition bearing code number 61/1041/97/2010 for analysis. As per PW-4 he conducted chemical analysis of the said sample and prepared his report dated 08.12.2010 which is Ex. PW 1/F. He also deposed that after analysis it was found that the sample was misbranded because there was violation of Rule 32 c(iii), Rule 32(i) and Rule 65-BB of PFA Act and Rule 1955. The witness was not cross-examined despite opportunity. 11. No other witness was examined and PE was closed. Thereafter, all the incriminating evidence was put to the accused and his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. was recorded. Accused also stated that several customer were present at the time of inspection but none was asked to join the investigation. He CC No:- 44284/2016 DA (FSO) v. Adesh Bansal Page No. 6 of 14 stated that he was neither the manufacturer nor the sample was packed or any impression of branding was done by him. He further stated that he had provided the bills from where he had purchased the sample to the officials but they had not investigated further on the same issue. He also stated that he is the owner of the departmental store where items come in a packed form and he had sold the same to the customers. No evidence in defence was led by the accused and the matter was listed for final arguments.
texts.arguments: 12. Ld. SPP for the complainant has argued that the complainant has been able to prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt, as all the witnesses have supported the case and there is no contradiction in their testimony. It is submitted that the accused has failed to rebut the findings as given by the PA. 13. Counsel for the accused on the other hand argued that accused is neither the manufacturer or packer of the food sample and is only a retailer of the food article. He further argued that the quantity of food article was purchased in bulk and the label of the food sample has not been placed on record. It was further argued by Ld. Counsel for accused that accused had no knowledge of the violation complained of in the present case. 19. Further misbranded is defined under the act as follows:- "misbranded" - an article of food shall be deemed to be misbranded- (a) **** (b) **** CC No:- 44284/2016 DA (FSO) v. Adesh Bansal Page No. 9 of 14 (c) **** (d) **** (e) **** (f) **** (g) **** (h) **** (i) **** (j) **** (k) if it is not labelled in accordance with the requirement of this Act or rule made thereunder...." Prohibitions of manufacture, sale, etc., of certain articles of food.- No personal shall himself or by any person on his behalf manufacture (for sale, or store, sell or distribute- (i) any adulterated food; (ii) any misbranded food; (iii) any article of food for the sale of which a licence is prescribed, except in accordance with the conditions of the licence; (iv) any article of food the sale of which is for the time being prohibited by the food (Health) Authority [in the interest of public health] (v) any article of food in contravention of any other person provision of this Act or of any rule made thereunder; (vi) any adulterant.." 21. DA (FSO) v. Adesh Bansal Page No. 11 of 14 25. Rule 32 of The Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 read as under: Rule 32. Every prepackaged food to carry a label:- (a) **** (b) **** (c) **** (i) **** (ii) **** (iii) Where an article of food is imported into India, the package of food shall also carry the name and complete address of the importer in India: 26. Rule 32 (i) read as follows:- (i) the month and year in capital letters upto which the product is best for consumption, in the following manner, namely:- " BEST BEFORE ............... MONTHS AND YEAR" "BEST BEFORE ............... MONTHS FROM PACKAGING" "BEST BEFORE ............... MONTHS FROM MANUFACTURE" OR [For "BEST BEFORE UPTO MONTH AND YEAR ..............." the period upto OR and BEST BEFORE WITHIN ............... MONTHS FROM inclusive THE DATE OF PACKAGING/MANUFACTURE" of 1st September, 2001] 27. Rule 64-BB. Extraneous addition of flavoring agents to be mentioned on the label:- " Where an extraneous flavouring agent has been added to any article of food, there shall be written just beneath the list of ingredients on the label, attached to any package of food so flavored, a statement in capital letters as below:- CONTAINS ADDED FLAVOUR (specify type of flavoring agent as per rule 63) CC No:- 44284/2016 DA (FSO) v. Adesh Bansal Page No. 12 of 14 Complainant vs Adesh Bansal on 26 July, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22060283/ 7 28. In P. K. Tejani v. M. r. Dange, (1974) CrLJ 313 (SC), Justice Krishna Iyer observed that in food offences strict liability is the rule not merely under IPC but all over the world.
